summary: Net +0.1 on w11 (8.1). Trim B on the centre block's aisle seats (D/G) is correct and convincing. In q13 the petal print on the D column against py_37302's foreground D seat is the best fabric match the PY area has had. The navy over-top strip is gone, the seat-pan bar is grey, the console side panel is dark, and the ear dash rows are gone. Two things hold the score down. (1) The trim A back/cushion weave was 'calmed' too far. Luminance std on the back fell from 31 to 19 (p4) and from 25 to 16 (p8), and bright-float coverage fell from 6 % to 0.4 %. py_37301/37305 are at std 35-48 with about 10 % bright floats. At cabin distance the window-pair and centre seats now read as a flat grey-blue mottle, not the ANA float weave, and close up (p5) it is still horizontal pixel streaks. (2) The literature pocket is better (smile rim, dark recess) but still has the wrong layout. The recess is about 0.77 of the screen-frame width (san_26 about 0.62). The tray hangs in the upper half of the recess with a straight black mesh slot under it, and about 0.11 m of plain shell is left below. In san_26 the tray and curved mesh sit at the bottom of the recess, which reaches almost to the lower edge of the shell.
lighting_note: Not scored. In studio p8 the back reads at V0.52 against the cushion's V0.78 (py_37301: back 0.70, cushion 0.71). Vertical fabric faces are under-lit relative to horizontal ones, which also hides weave contrast. In q13 the navy flap is #38446e against py_37302's #283769, which is fine. The p4 studio flap is #273053, darker than every photo (studio light).

issues.fix: test/make_swatches.py synth_py_back. Keep the thread floats and tapered ends, but restore contrast. Change `lite *= 0.45 + 0.85 * thr` to `0.7 + 0.6 * thr` (the thread modulation currently roughly halves the float brightness) and `out = (1 + 1.4 * lite)` to `(1 + 2.2 * lite)`. Raise float coverage by widening the light band half-width 3.6 -> 4.2. Target rendered back std/mean about 0.25 and (p95-p5)/mean about 0.8 in p8. Blur the brick-patch lattice mask (line 139 onward) by about 4-6 px with _blur_wrap so no square block edges remain. Re-run make_swatches and keep pyFabric's base #7e8593 so the mean colour holds. If the shader mip blurs the floats away (p8 gx 7 against 20 in the photo), lower the tile repeat slightly rather than the contrast.
